- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect mean reversion or sentiment reversal.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overreacts and forecasts continued ascent; cap forecast growth to avoid lagged overcorrection.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; apply a downward bias to forecast horizon.
- Model tends to underpredict true price peaks in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed or volatile; add 1–2% buffer to forecast if sentiment shows upward momentum.
- If recent history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline), model often ignores it; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day of negative sentiment trend.
